solution:
The boundary line is \(x = 0\), which is the Y-axis.
The inequation \(x \ge 0\) is satisfied by every point whose \(x\)-coordinate is greater than or equal to \(0\).
Check a point on the right, say \((1, 0)\): \(x = 1 \ge 0\), true. So the required region lies to the right of the Y-axis.
Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line \(x = 0\) (the Y-axis) is included.
Solution set: the right half-plane, i.e. all points on and to the right of the Y-axis. It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of x ≥ 0 (right of the Y-axis)

solution:
The boundary line is \(x = 0\), which is the Y-axis.
The inequation \(x \le 0\) is satisfied by every point whose \(x\)-coordinate is less than or equal to \(0\).
Check a point on the left, say \((-1, 0)\): \(x = -1 \le 0\), true. So the required region lies to the left of the Y-axis.
Since the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line \(x = 0\) (the Y-axis) is included.
Solution set: the left half-plane, i.e. all points on and to the left of the Y-axis. It is an unbounded region.

solution:
The boundary line is \(y = 0\), which is the X-axis.
The inequation \(y \ge 0\) is satisfied by every point whose \(y\)-coordinate is greater than or equal to \(0\).
Check a point above, say \((0, 1)\): \(y = 1 \ge 0\), true. So the required region lies above the X-axis.
Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line \(y = 0\) (the X-axis) is included.
Solution set: the upper half-plane, i.e. all points on and above the X-axis. It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of y ≥ 0 (above the X-axis)

solution:
The boundary line is \(y = 0\), which is the X-axis.
The inequation \(y \le 0\) is satisfied by every point whose \(y\)-coordinate is less than or equal to \(0\).
Check a point below, say \((0, -1)\): \(y = -1 \le 0\), true. So the required region lies below the X-axis.
Since the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line \(y = 0\) (the X-axis) is included.
Solution set: the lower half-plane, i.e. all points on and below the X-axis. It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of y ≤ 0 (below the X-axis)

solution:
Boundary lines: \(x = 0\) (Y-axis) and \(y = 0\) (X-axis).
\(x \ge 0\): the region on and to the right of the Y-axis (contains \((1,0)\)).
\(y \ge 0\): the region on and above the X-axis (contains \((0,1)\)).
The solution set is the intersection of these two half-planes.
Both boundaries are included (inequalities are \(\ge\)).
Solution set: the first quadrant, i.e. all points with \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0 (first quadrant)

solution:
Boundary lines: \(x = 0\) (Y-axis) and \(y = 0\) (X-axis).
\(x \le 0\): the region on and to the left of the Y-axis (contains \((-1,0)\)).
\(y \ge 0\): the region on and above the X-axis (contains \((0,1)\)).
The solution set is the intersection of these two half-planes.
Both boundaries are included.
Solution set: the second quadrant, i.e. all points with \(x \le 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). It is an unbounded region.

solution:
Boundary lines: \(x = 0\) (Y-axis) and \(y = 0\) (X-axis).
\(x \le 0\): the region on and to the left of the Y-axis (contains \((-1,0)\)).
\(y \le 0\): the region on and below the X-axis (contains \((0,-1)\)).
The solution set is the intersection of these two half-planes.
Both boundaries are included.
Solution set: the third quadrant, i.e. all points with \(x \le 0\) and \(y \le 0\). It is an unbounded region.

solution:
Boundary lines: \(x = 0\) (Y-axis) and \(y = 0\) (X-axis).
\(x \ge 0\): the region on and to the right of the Y-axis (contains \((1,0)\)).
\(y \le 0\): the region on and below the X-axis (contains \((0,-1)\)).
The solution set is the intersection of these two half-planes.
Both boundaries are included.
Solution set: the fourth quadrant, i.e. all points with \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \le 0\). It is an unbounded region.

solution:
\(2x - 3 \ge 0\) gives \(x \ge \dfrac{3}{2}\).
The boundary line is \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\), a vertical line parallel to the Y-axis.
Test the origin \((0,0)\): \(2(0) - 3 = -3 \ge 0\) is false, so the origin does NOT lie in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane on the side away from the origin, i.e. to the right of the line \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\).
Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\) is included.
Solution set: all points on and to the right of \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 2x − 3 ≥ 0, i.e. x ≥ 3/2

solution:
\(2y - 5 \ge 0\) gives \(y \ge \dfrac{5}{2}\).
The boundary line is \(y = \dfrac{5}{2}\), a horizontal line parallel to the X-axis.
Test the origin \((0,0)\): \(2(0) - 5 = -5 \ge 0\) is false, so the origin does NOT lie in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane on the side away from the origin, i.e. above the line \(y = \dfrac{5}{2}\).
Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line \(y = \dfrac{5}{2}\) is included.
Solution set: all points on and above \(y = \dfrac{5}{2}\). It is an unbounded region.

solution:
\(3x + 4 \le 0\) gives \(x \le -\dfrac{4}{3}\).
The boundary line is \(x = -\dfrac{4}{3}\), a vertical line parallel to the Y-axis.
Test the origin \((0,0)\): \(3(0) + 4 = 4 \le 0\) is false, so the origin does NOT lie in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane on the side away from the origin, i.e. to the left of the line \(x = -\dfrac{4}{3}\).
Since the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line \(x = -\dfrac{4}{3}\) is included.
Solution set: all points on and to the left of \(x = -\dfrac{4}{3}\). It is an unbounded region.

solution:
\(5y + 3 \le 0\) gives \(y \le -\dfrac{3}{5}\).
The boundary line is \(y = -\dfrac{3}{5}\), a horizontal line parallel to the X-axis.
Test the origin \((0,0)\): \(5(0) + 3 = 3 \le 0\) is false, so the origin does NOT lie in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane on the side away from the origin, i.e. below the line \(y = -\dfrac{3}{5}\).
Since the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line \(y = -\dfrac{3}{5}\) is included.
Solution set: all points on and below \(y = -\dfrac{3}{5}\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 5y + 3 ≤ 0, i.e. y ≤ −3/5

solution:
Boundary line: \(x + 2y = 6\).
Intercepts: put \(y = 0\) to get \(x = 6\), so \((6, 0)\); put \(x = 0\) to get \(2y = 6\), i.e. \(y = 3\), so \((0, 3)\).
Test the origin \((0,0)\): \(0 + 2(0) = 0 \le 6\) is true, so the origin lies in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane containing the origin, i.e. below the line \(x + 2y = 6\).
Since the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line is included.
Solution set: all points on and on the origin side of \(x + 2y = 6\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of x + 2y ≤ 6

solution:
Boundary line: \(2x - 5y = 10\).
Intercepts: put \(y = 0\) to get \(2x = 10\), i.e. \(x = 5\), so \((5, 0)\); put \(x = 0\) to get \(-5y = 10\), i.e. \(y = -2\), so \((0, -2)\).
Test the origin \((0,0)\): \(2(0) - 5(0) = 0 \ge 10\) is false, so the origin does NOT lie in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane on the side away from the origin, i.e. below-right of the line \(2x - 5y = 10\).
Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line is included.
Solution set: all points on and on the non-origin side of \(2x - 5y = 10\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 2x − 5y ≥ 10

solution:
Boundary line: \(3x + 2y = 0\). This line passes through the origin, so the origin cannot be used as a test point.
Two points on the line: \((0, 0)\) and \((2, -3)\) (since \(3(2) + 2(-3) = 0\)). The line has slope \(-\dfrac{3}{2}\).
Test another point not on the line, say \((1, 0)\): \(3(1) + 2(0) = 3 \ge 0\) is true, so \((1, 0)\) lies in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane containing \((1, 0)\), i.e. the side of the line \(3x + 2y = 0\) towards the positive X-axis.
Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line is included.
Solution set: all points on and on the \((1,0)\) side of \(3x + 2y = 0\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 3x + 2y ≥ 0 (line through origin)

solution:
Boundary line: \(5x - 3y = 0\). This line passes through the origin, so the origin cannot be used as a test point.
Two points on the line: \((0, 0)\) and \((3, 5)\) (since \(5(3) - 3(5) = 0\)). The line has slope \(\dfrac{5}{3}\).
Test another point not on the line, say \((0, 1)\): \(5(0) - 3(1) = -3 \le 0\) is true, so \((0, 1)\) lies in the region.
Hence the required region is the half-plane containing \((0, 1)\), i.e. the side of the line \(5x - 3y = 0\) towards the positive Y-axis.
Since the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line is included.
Solution set: all points on and on the \((0,1)\) side of \(5x - 3y = 0\). It is an unbounded region.

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 5x − 3y ≤ 0 (line through origin)

solution:
First inequation \(2x + y \ge 2\). Boundary \(2x + y = 2\); intercepts \((1, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(2(0) + 0 = 0 \ge 2\) is false, so the region is the half-plane NOT containing the origin (above-right of the line), boundary included.

Second inequation \(x - y \le 1\). Boundary \(x - y = 1\); intercepts \((1, 0)\) and \((0, -1)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 - 0 = 0 \le 1\) is true, so the region is the half-plane containing the origin (above-left of the line), boundary included.

The two boundary lines meet where \(2x + y = 2\) and \(x - y = 1\). Adding: \(3x = 3\), so \(x = 1\), \(y = 0\); they intersect at \((1, 0)\).
Solution set: the intersection of the two half-planes, an unbounded region with corner \((1, 0)\).

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 2x + y ≥ 2 and x − y ≤ 1

solution:
First inequation \(x - y \le 2\). Boundary \(x - y = 2\); intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((0, -2)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 - 0 = 0 \le 2\) is true, so the region is the half-plane containing the origin (above-left of the line), boundary included.

Second inequation \(x + 2y \le 8\). Boundary \(x + 2y = 8\); intercepts \((8, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 + 2(0) = 0 \le 8\) is true, so the region is the half-plane containing the origin (below-left of the line), boundary included.

The two boundary lines meet where \(x - y = 2\) and \(x + 2y = 8\). Subtracting: \(3y = 6\), so \(y = 2\), \(x = 4\); they intersect at \((4, 2)\).
Solution set: the intersection of the two half-planes (the region containing the origin), an unbounded region with corner \((4, 2)\).

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of x − y ≤ 2 and x + 2y ≤ 8

solution:
First inequation \(x + y \ge 6\). Boundary \(x + y = 6\); intercepts \((6, 0)\) and \((0, 6)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 + 0 = 0 \ge 6\) is false, so the region is the half-plane NOT containing the origin (above-right of the line), boundary included.

Second inequation \(x + 2y \le 10\). Boundary \(x + 2y = 10\); intercepts \((10, 0)\) and \((0, 5)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 + 2(0) = 0 \le 10\) is true, so the region is the half-plane containing the origin (below-left of the line), boundary included.

The two boundary lines meet where \(x + y = 6\) and \(x + 2y = 10\). Subtracting: \(y = 4\), so \(x = 2\); they intersect at \((2, 4)\).
Solution set: the intersection of the two half-planes (points that are above \(x + y = 6\) yet below \(x + 2y = 10\)), an unbounded region with corner \((2, 4)\).

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of x + y ≥ 6 and x + 2y ≤ 10

solution:
First inequation \(2x + 3y \le 6\). Boundary \(2x + 3y = 6\); intercepts \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(2(0) + 3(0) = 0 \le 6\) is true, so the region is the half-plane containing the origin (below-left of the line), boundary included.

Second inequation \(x + 4y \ge 4\). Boundary \(x + 4y = 4\); intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 1)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 + 4(0) = 0 \ge 4\) is false, so the region is the half-plane NOT containing the origin (above-right of the line), boundary included.

The two boundary lines meet where \(2x + 3y = 6\) and \(x + 4y = 4\). From the second, \(x = 4 - 4y\); substituting: \(2(4 - 4y) + 3y = 6\), i.e. \(8 - 8y + 3y = 6\), \(-5y = -2\), \(y = \dfrac{2}{5}\), and \(x = 4 - 4\cdot\dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{12}{5}\); they intersect at \(\left(\dfrac{12}{5}, \dfrac{2}{5}\right)\).
Solution set: the intersection of the two half-planes (below \(2x + 3y = 6\) and above \(x + 4y = 4\)), a region with corner \(\left(\dfrac{12}{5}, \dfrac{2}{5}\right)\).

diagramSpec.caption: Solution region of 2x + 3y ≤ 6 and x + 4y ≥ 4

solution:
First inequation \(2x + y \ge 5\). Boundary \(2x + y = 5\); intercepts \(\left(\dfrac{5}{2}, 0\right)\) and \((0, 5)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(2(0) + 0 = 0 \ge 5\) is false, so the region is the half-plane NOT containing the origin (above-right of the line), boundary included.

Second inequation \(x - y \le 1\). Boundary \(x - y = 1\); intercepts \((1, 0)\) and \((0, -1)\).
Test \((0,0)\): \(0 - 0 = 0 \le 1\) is true, so the region is the half-plane containing the origin (above-left of the line), boundary included.

The two boundary lines meet where \(2x + y = 5\) and \(x - y = 1\). Adding: \(3x = 6\), so \(x = 2\), \(y = 1\); they intersect at \((2, 1)\).
Solution set: the intersection of the two half-planes, an unbounded region with corner \((2, 1)\).
